title: Sauvignon Blanc
description: Also called Fumé Blanc. Grass, gooseberry and passion fruit, from the Loire to Marlborough.
L: Describe Sauvignon Blanc's flavours and structure

Sauvignon Blanc gives crisp, aromatic whites with gooseberry, lime, grapefruit, passion fruit, cut grass, green pepper, elderflower and sometimes a flinty or smoky note. Acidity is high, body light to medium. Most is unoaked and drunk young. It's one of the most recognisable white grapes.

Sauvignon Blanc probably comes from the Loire or Bordeaux; its name may come from sauvage, wild, for its vigorous growth. DNA shows a close link to Savagnin, of the Traminer family. Crossed with Cabernet Franc, it gave Cabernet Sauvignon in 17th century Bordeaux. It buds late and ripens early.
Which famous red grape is Sauvignon Blanc a parent of?
Sauvignon Blanc crossed with Cabernet Franc gave Cabernet Sauvignon.

Look for pale lemon-green colour, an intense nose of gooseberry, grass and citrus, sometimes tropical fruit, and a crisp, mouth-watering palate. Compared with Riesling, it's more green and herbal, less floral; compared with Chardonnay, much more aromatic and usually unoaked.
Most Sauvignon Blanc is aged in new oak.
Not true. Most is unoaked, to keep its fresh aromas.
Sauvignon Blanc gives gooseberry, grass and citrus
It's a parent of Cabernet Sauvignon
It's crisp, aromatic and usually unoaked
From the Loire to the world

Sauvignon Blanc's French homes are the Loire, especially Sancerre and Pouilly-Fumé, and Bordeaux, blended with Sémillon. New Zealand's Marlborough made it world-famous. Chile's coastal valleys, like Casablanca and Leyda, South Africa's Elgin and Durbanville, California, Austria's Styria and north-east Italy also grow it.

Sauvignon Blanc needs a cool or moderate climate to keep its acidity and aromas. Cool sites give green, grassy, citrus styles; warmer ones give tropical, passion fruit and melon. Too much heat makes it flat and loses its aromas. Coastal influence and altitude help in warmer countries.
Cool for green; warmer for tropical
Match each region to its Sauvignon style.
Climate and tradition shape each style.

Sauvignon's green notes come from methoxypyrazines, highest in cool sites and shaded fruit. Its tropical notes come from thiols, like 3MH, smelling of passion fruit and grapefruit, released from precursors during fermentation. Winemakers can boost thiols with machine harvesting, skin contact and specific yeasts.
Which compounds give Sauvignon's passion fruit aroma?
Sauvignon grows in the Loire, Bordeaux, New Zealand and beyond
Cool sites give green notes; warmer ones tropical
Pyrazines give grass; thiols give passion fruit

Sancerre, on the left bank of the upper Loire, makes 100% Sauvignon Blanc whites from hillside vineyards. Its style is crisp and restrained, with citrus, gooseberry, white flowers and a mineral, flinty edge. Sancerre also makes red and rosé from Pinot Noir. Nearby Menetou-Salon, Quincy and Reuilly make similar wines.

Three soils shape Sancerre: terres blanches, Kimmeridgian clay-limestone, giving full, structured wines; caillottes, stony limestone, giving fresh, aromatic wines; and silex, flint, giving smoky, mineral, long-lived wines. Pouilly-Fumé, across the river, is known for its flint and a smoky, gunflint character, hence fumé, smoky.
Match each soil to its Sancerre style.
Didier Dagueneau, in Pouilly-Fumé, made some of the world's most celebrated Sauvignon Blanc, showing how long it can age from great sites.
What does fumé in Pouilly-Fumé refer to?
Fumé means smoky, linked to its flint soils and the grape's bloom.
Sancerre is crisp, restrained and mineral
Terres blanches, caillottes and silex give different styles
Pouilly-Fumé is known for smoky, flinty wines

Marlborough, at the north-east tip of New Zealand's South Island, has long, sunny days, high UV light and cold nights. That combination gives intensely aromatic Sauvignon with ripe tropical fruit and piercing acidity at the same time. Stony, free-draining soils in the Wairau Valley help.
Sun by day, cold by night

Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc is explosive: passion fruit, gooseberry, grapefruit, cut grass and green pepper, with high acidity. Cloudy Bay's 1985 vintage made it famous worldwide. Today Sauvignon Blanc is about 60% of New Zealand's vineyards and over 80% of its exports.
Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc became world-famous with Cloudy Bay's ____ vintage.
Cloudy Bay's 1985 launched the Marlborough style.

Marlborough isn't one style. The Wairau Valley gives classic tropical, aromatic wines; the Awatere Valley, cooler and windier, gives more herbal, mineral, saline wines. Some producers use barrel fermentation, wild yeast or lees ageing for more complex, textured versions.
Most Marlborough Sauvignon is unoaked and fresh.
Marlborough's sun and cold nights give intense, fresh Sauvignon
The Awatere gives a cooler, more herbal style

In Bordeaux, Sauvignon Blanc is blended with Sémillon, sometimes Muscadelle. Sauvignon brings acidity and aroma; Sémillon body and texture. Pessac-Léognan makes the finest dry whites, often fermented and aged in oak, which can age 20 years. Entre-Deux-Mers makes fresh, unoaked versions. Sauvignon is also part of sweet Sauternes.

In 1966, Robert Mondavi in California named his oak-aged Sauvignon Blanc Fumé Blanc, borrowing from Pouilly-Fumé, to sell a then-unpopular grape. It worked. Today Fumé Blanc in the US often, but not always, means an oaked Sauvignon. The term isn't legally defined.
Who created the name Fumé Blanc?

In Sauternes, Sauvignon adds acidity and freshness to botrytised Sémillon. In Styria, Austria, and Friuli, Italy, Sauvignon is made in a mineral, sometimes oak-aged style. Chile's Leyda and South Africa's Elgin give fresh, coastal versions.
Fumé Blanc is a legally defined style.
Not true. It's a marketing term, often but not always meaning an oaked Sauvignon.
Bordeaux blends Sauvignon with Sémillon, often oaked
Fumé Blanc was Mondavi's 1966 marketing name

Sauvignon Blanc suits goat's cheese, a Loire classic with Sancerre, salads, green vegetables, asparagus, herbs, seafood, sushi and Thai dishes with lime and coriander. Its acidity cuts through fried food. Oaked Bordeaux whites suit richer fish and white meat.
Serve at 7 to 10 degrees. Most Sauvignon Blanc is best within one to three years. Top Sancerre, Pouilly-Fumé and Pessac-Léognan can age 10 to 20 years, gaining honey, smoke and mineral notes.
Which cheese is a classic Loire match for Sancerre?
Crottin de Chavignol comes from a village in Sancerre.
Sauvignon Blanc's green notes make it one of the few wines that pairs with asparagus and green salads.
Sauvignon suits goat's cheese, greens and herbs
Top Loire and Bordeaux wines age 10 to 20 years
Match each region to its style.
Each place shows a different side.
Which compounds give Sauvignon its grassy, green pepper notes?
Methoxypyrazines, highest in cool, shaded sites.
Sauvignon Blanc is a parent of Cabernet Sauvignon.
Cloudy Bay's 1985 vintage made ____ Sauvignon Blanc famous.
Sauvignon Blanc is crisp, green and aromatic
Sancerre and Marlborough are its benchmarks
It suits goat's cheese, greens and herbs
